title: Cyrus and the Horizon
premise: Astrid Brightwater, a clone who inherited the original's unsolved murder case and the debts that came with it, has spent ten years hauling cargo through contested orbits under a name that isn't legally his. When a distress signal arrives in a language extinct for two centuries, he traces it to a derelict relay at the edge of dead space and discovers the murdered original was investigating a corporate conspiracy to erase an entire colony's records—and its people. Racing rival salvagers, corporate enforcers, and his own failing clone-body warranty, Astrid must decide whether justice outside the law is worth the last of his borrowed life. In the end he broadcasts the colony's testimony to every open channel, exposes the corporation, and dies in the cold of the relay—only for the epilogue's rescue crews to find a backup of him hidden in the signal itself.
about_author: J. M. Eastwick is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade listening to voices fade out over open water before turning to fiction. They write about people who inherit other people's problems and call it survival.

chapters.title: Dead Channels
chapters.summary: Astrid Brightwater's POV. Hauling ore through contested orbits, Astrid fields a routine customs shakedown that reminds him his legal identity is ten years from expiring with his clone warranty. Emotional beat: weary resignation masking old anger.

chapters.title: The Inheritance
chapters.summary: Flashback woven into present-tense loading dock work. Astrid recalls waking in a vat with the original's memories, his murder case, and his creditors. Emotional beat: grief for a self he never chose.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Alone on night watch, Astrid intercepts a repeating distress transmission in Old Meridian—a language extinct since the Colony Wars. His translation software fails; his inherited memories don't. Emotional beat: electric unease.

chapters.title: Cargo Contract
chapters.summary: Astrid takes a suspiciously well-paid contract routing near dead space, suspecting the client wants his ship, not his cargo. First hint someone else heard the signal too. Emotional beat: wary greed wrestling instinct.

chapters.title: The Original's Files
chapters.summary: Digging through encrypted archives inherited with his body, Astrid finds the original had been hired by Meridian survivors' descendants before his murder. Emotional beat: dawning purpose.

chapters.title: Rivals on the Lane
chapters.summary: POV shift: Vess Karrow, captain of a rival salvage crew, is offered a bounty on any ship answering the dead-space signal. She takes it without asking what it is. Emotional beat: pragmatic ruthlessness.

chapters.title: Border of Dead Space
chapters.summary: Astrid crosses into the silence beyond the beacon network, where no law reaches and no rescue follows. The ship feels smaller with every light-year. Emotional beat: isolation sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Ghost Relay
chapters.summary: He finds the relay—intact, powered, impossible. Someone has maintained it for two centuries. Inside, fresh air and a warm cup of tea. Emotional beat: uncanny dread.

chapters.title: The Keeper
chapters.summary: Astrid meets Sefa, an elderly woman raised aboard the relay by generations of caretakers, speaking only Old Meridian. She's been sending the distress call for forty years. Emotional beat: cautious connection across time.

chapters.title: What Was Erased
chapters.summary: Sefa shows him the archive: the colony Meridian wasn't lost—it was deleted, its population indentured and its records burned by Halcyon Combine. The original knew. Emotional beat: cold fury.

chapters.title: Murder, Reopened
chapters.summary: Astrid matches the original's case file to the archive: the murder wasn't random. The original had proof. Somewhere aboard or in orbit, that proof may still exist. Emotional beat: vengeful clarity.

chapters.title: Vess Arrives
chapters.summary: Karrow's salvage crew docks, ostensibly friendly. Her engineer recognizes the relay's value; her sponsor wants witnesses erased. Tense dinner scene. Emotional beat: coiled diplomacy.

chapters.title: The Bargain
chapters.summary: Astrid offers Karrow a cut of the archive's historical value if she helps broadcast it. She counters: she wants the bounty on whoever killed the original. Uneasy alliance formed. Emotional beat: transactional trust.

chapters.title: Enforcers
chapters.summary: Halcyon enforcement vessel detected inbound. Sefa reveals the relay can mask signals—but broadcasting will unmask them permanently. Emotional beat: ticking clock established.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: One of Karrow's crew, secretly on Halcyon payroll, cripples the relay's transmitter array. Astrid catches him mid-act; a brutal, close-quarters fight in zero-g. Emotional beat: betrayal made physical.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: POV: the saboteur, Drenn, under questioning. He reveals Halcyon has been hunting Meridian descendants for decades—not for records, but because some survived the erasure. Emotional beat: horror compounding.

chapters.title: Survivors
chapters.summary: Sefa admits she isn't alone: eleven others live in the relay's deep compartments, children of the erased colony, stateless and undocumented. Astrid realizes he's responsible for lives now. Emotional beat: reluctant guardianship.

chapters.title: Repair Under Deadline
chapters.summary: Montage chapter: Astrid and Karrow's engineer rebuild the transmitter while the enforcer ship burns toward them. Karrow and Astrid trade histories over solder fumes. Emotional beat: camaraderie forged under pressure.

chapters.title: The Warranty
chapters.summary: Astrid's clone body begins failing early—headaches, memory stutter. Using the relay's ancient medical bay, he learns the truth: Halcyon holds his clone license, and they've flagged him. Emotional beat: mortality weaponized against him.

chapters.title: They Know My Name
chapters.summary: A Halcyon transmission addresses 'Brightwater' by name, offering amnesty for the archive and the survivors. It confirms the original was murdered on their order. Emotional beat: terror and confirmation entwined.

chapters.title: Vote
chapters.summary: Astrid puts it to the survivors: hide forever, or broadcast and become targets. A young survivor, Ilo, votes to be seen. The room follows. Emotional beat: courage chosen collectively.

chapters.title: First Broadcast
chapters.summary: Partial transmission goes out before the array overheats—enough for one listening station to log fragments. Halcyon's enforcer changes course directly for them. Emotional beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Running Dark
chapters.summary: Astrid attempts to tow the relay's core archive onto his cargo hauler. Engineering nightmare in dead space, no gravity, no margin. Emotional beat: desperate competence.

chapters.title: Karrow's Choice
chapters.summary: POV: Karrow. Her sponsor orders her to abandon Astrid and take the archive herself. She looks at the survivors' faces and refuses—for the first time choosing a side. Emotional beat: corruption resisted.

chapters.title: Boarders
chapters.summary: Halcyon enforcers board under pretense of inspection. A standoff in the relay corridor; Sefa speaks to their commander in Old Meridian, and one young enforcer translates, visibly shaken—he's Meridian-descended too. Emotional beat: the erased recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: The young enforcer, Tam, defects mid-standoff, triggering a firefight. Drenn escapes custody in the chaos. Casualties among the survivors. Emotional beat: cost made blood-real.

chapters.title: Burial in the Silence
chapters.summary: Quiet chapter: funerals held in the relay's observation dome, bodies given to the dark. Astrid reads the names of the erased colony aloud—the first time in two centuries anyone has. Emotional beat: mourning as resistance.

chapters.title: The Proof
chapters.summary: Following the original's encrypted trail, Astrid finds the murder evidence sealed inside the relay's foundation: orders, signatures, and the original's final testimony naming his killer—now a Halcyon director. Emotional beat: the case closes itself.

chapters.title: Drenn's Revenge
chapters.summary: Drenn sabotages the hauler's drive and takes two survivors hostage, demanding extraction. Astrid talks him down—or talks him out an airlock; the text keeps it ambiguous even to Astrid. Emotional beat: justice's ugly edge.

chapters.title: Last Fuel
chapters.summary: With the drive limping and fuel nearly gone, Astrid calculates he can reach the edge of patrolled space OR transmit at full power—not both. Karrow offers her ship's reserves. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered freely.

chapters.title: Convergence
chapters.summary: Every faction converges on the relay: Halcyon fleet, independent press ship tipped by the fragment broadcast, and colonial militia descended from other erased settlements. Emotional beat: the silence ending everywhere at once.

chapters.title: The Director
chapters.summary: POV: Director Hale, the original's murderer, arrives demanding surrender, offering Astrid a new body, a new identity, everything—in exchange for the archive. Astrid hears his own original's voice in the refusal he gives. Emotional beat: temptation declined.

chapters.title: Full Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax begins: the repaired array fires the complete archive—testimony, orders, names of the living and the dead—to every open channel. Halcyon opens fire on the relay. Emotional beat: triumph and terror simultaneous.

chapters.title: Holding the Line
chapters.summary: Karrow's ship and defecting militia draw Halcyon fire while the transmission completes. Astrid stays at the console, body failing, hand on the send key until the progress bar fills. Emotional beat: stubborn endurance unto death.

chapters.title: Cyrus and the Horizon
chapters.summary: Title drop: Sefa's word for the relay—'cyrus,' the horizon you walk toward and never reach. As the fleet breaches the dome, Astrid watches the transmission light up distant stations like dawn. Emotional beat: transcendence in defeat.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Halcyon collapses under public reckoning; warrants issue, including for Hale, who flees. Karrow claims salvage rights over the relay and becomes its unlikely protector. Emotional beat: justice arriving late but arriving.

chapters.title: Cold
chapters.summary: Rescue crews find Astrid's body at the console, warranty expired, expression calm. The survivors refuse to let him be logged as unnamed property. Emotional beat: grief with dignity.

chapters.title: The Backup
chapters.summary: Sefa reveals the relay archived Astrid's neural pattern during his medical scan—a complete backup, illegal, unprecedented. The survivors vote unanimously to wake him. Emotional beat: hope smuggled past death.

chapters.title: New Registration
chapters.summary: Final chapter: Astrid wakes, legally nonexistent and finally free of the original's debts and name. He registers himself—first entry in the restored Meridian census—as Cyrus Brightwater, and points his ship at the horizon. Emotional beat: rebirth on his own terms.
